visual_blocks.heading: ORIGINAL MCQ MASTERY SET - EXACTLY 48 QUESTIONS
visual_blocks.preview: Questions 1-40 are core coverage - four per subtopic across the ten subtopics; Questions 41-48 are remedial items targeting the most common misreadings. Correct answers rotate strictly A -> B -> C -> D 12 times.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 1 - Humanism I: Dignity, Agency and the Human-Centred Argument
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: define -> distinguish from the nearest look-alike -> three-step argument -> one named anchor (H1) -> limit-specifying verdict. Never celebrate the value; specify what it cannot do.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 2 - Humanism II: Genealogy and Forms (Renaissance, Enlightenment, Branches)
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: tenets (DRAF + forms) -> five paving steps -> "decisive articulation, not the sole source" qualification. The qualification is the mark-separator.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 3 - Humanism III: Indian Humanism and Its Critics (Tagore, Gandhi, Vivekananda, Roy)
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: for any Indian-humanism stem, pick a NAMED ground (Tagore relation / Gandhi non-violence / Roy autonomy), then add the structural supplement (Ambedkar/Marx). The supplement is the evaluation.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 4 - Secularism I: Secular, Secularisation, Secularism and the Core Argument
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: fix the meaning (adjective/process/doctrine) -> two freedoms (of AND from) -> two failure-modes (state capture / community immunity) -> equal citizenship is the end, separation only a means.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 5 - Secularism II: Western Models and the Secularism-Pluralism Relation
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: name the model + device + strength + risk; for pluralism stems run the three decoupling cases; keep "necessary" (conceptual) apart from "coexists" (historical).

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 6 - Secularism III: Indian Secularism, Principled Distance and Its Critics
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: expound before you evaluate; hold 1976/1994 as illustration not proof; Gandhi (ethical religion) + Ambedkar (constitutional morality) + Bhargava (institutional distance) is the Indian secular-democracy triangle.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 7 - Multiculturalism I: Recognition, Group-Differentiated Rights and Dialogue
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: define normatively (recognition + accommodation), then split descriptive (fact of diversity) from normative (justice of recognition); external protections = yes, internal restrictions = no is the criterion that earns the marks.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 8 - Multiculturalism II: India, Globalisation, Feminism and the Objections
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: run each objection with its reply; for tolerance stems climb the ladder to recognition; "who bears the cost?" is the feminist test; caste hierarchy is domination, not diversity.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 9 - Recognition and Redistribution: Fraser, Honneth and the Two Grammars of Justice
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: money vs esteem; Fraser (dual, parity of participation) vs Honneth (recognition foundational, three spheres); verdict = distinct-but-entangled; affirmative/transformative is the criterion for internal-restriction stems.

visual_blocks.heading: EXAM APPLICATION 10 - Synthesis and Limits: The Anthropocentric Boundary, Debates, Criticisms and Traps
visual_blocks.preview: 🔑 MEMORY: end humanism 20-markers on the ecological limit (state the residue); pick the §4 debate spine that matches the two names in the stem; name the REMAINING danger to turn a summary into a verdict.
